# Dictate
A local-only push-to-talk dictation service. Its supported pipeline is:
``` press → in-memory microphone capture → local whisper.cpp → local Ollama cleanup → target revalidation → insert or recovery ```
It has no cloud fallback, telemetry, web service, GUI, database, clipboard fallback, or default content history.
## Requirements
- Python 3.11 or newer - The package dependencies installed from `pyproject.toml`: `sounddevice` and `pynput` - A locally installed `whisper.cpp` server and local speech model - [Ollama](https://ollama.com/) running locally with `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M` acquired explicitly by the user - A microphone and platform permissions for microphone access, global keyboard monitoring, and verified text placement
Local runtime and model installation is a user-initiated setup operation. Normal dictation must work with the Internet disconnected after those local components are ready.
## Install
```bash python3 -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate python -m pip install -e . ollama pull qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M ```
Install `whisper.cpp` and its model using its local installation instructions, then start its loopback-only server. Do not configure either inference endpoint to a non-loopback address.
## Command contract
```bash dictate setup dictate devices dictate doctor dictate serve ```
- `setup` verifies the required local components and reports ready only when they are available. - `devices` lists local input identifiers and display names without recording. - `doctor` prints content-free readiness failures and platform-specific remediation. - `serve` starts the local push-to-talk pipeline only after required local readiness checks pass.
The repository's acceptance tests exercise the service through deterministic local boundaries. Current native adapters intentionally fail closed for automatic placement until they can verify the original text target, so `setup`, `doctor`, and `serve` correctly report placement as not ready on such a host. A pending unsafe-placement result remains in process memory only; an interactive recovery UX is not yet available.
## Blessed defaults
A fresh configuration uses one supported pipeline:
| Setting | Default | |---|---| | Microphone | `system-default` | | Trigger | `right_alt` | | Style | `Natural` | | Local ASR endpoint | `http://127.0.0.1:8080` | | Local Ollama endpoint | `http://127.0.0.1:11434` | | Cleanup model | `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M` | | Context limit | 1,024 characters |
The built-in cleanup styles are Natural, Formal, Casual, and Technical. Cleanup is mandatory, deterministic local Ollama processing; it transforms what was dictated and must not answer questions or add content.
## Privacy and safety
Audio, transcript, bounded destination context, dictionary terms, prompts, generated text, and a recovery result stay in memory for the active session. They are cleared after placement, failure, recovery consumption, timeout, or service exit. Ordinary logs and diagnostics contain status, timing, sizes, and error metadata only.
Both ASR and Ollama endpoints are validated as loopback-only before content can be sent. A remote endpoint is a hard configuration error, not a fallback choice.
Destination context is optional. If the platform cannot provide its bounded target-local context, diagnostics report the limitation and dictation proceeds without context. Screen capture, OCR, and collection from unrelated applications are not used.
Text is injected only after revalidating the original application, window, and text target captured at key-down. If that check fails, no destination receives text; the result is retained only in process memory pending an explicit recovery interaction.
## Platform behavior and validation
The cross-platform acceptance contract and the current content-free evidence are in [`specs/001-local-dictation/platform-acceptance-matrix.md`](specs/001-local-dictation/platform-acceptance-matrix.md). The generic key-monitoring path is shared. macOS, Windows, and Linux adapters fail closed for automatic placement until their platform has a verified original-target implementation; they report remediation rather than risking insertion into an unrelated field.
The warmed-model latency acceptance target is visible placement within five seconds of release for at least 90% of successful short dictations. The timing report carries only duration and outcome metadata.
## Validate
```bash PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -v ```
The acceptance suite includes offline socket blocking, focus safety, privacy lifecycle checks, the common platform matrix, and a deterministic synthetic short-audio latency fixture.

"""Directly editable TOML preferences with safe defaults."""
from __future__ import annotations
import os import tempfile import tomllib from dataclasses import dataclass from pathlib import Path
from dictate.privacy import validate_loopback_url
STYLES = ("Natural", "Formal", "Casual", "Technical") DEFAULT_TRIGGER = "right_alt" DEFAULT_OLLAMA_ENDPOINT = "http://127.0.0.1:11434" DEFAULT_ASR_ENDPOINT = "http://127.0.0.1:8080" DEFAULT_OLLAMA_MODEL = "qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M"
@dataclass(frozen=True) class Preferences: microphone: str = "system-default" trigger: str = DEFAULT_TRIGGER style: str = "Natural" asr_endpoint: str = DEFAULT_ASR_ENDPOINT ollama_endpoint: str = DEFAULT_OLLAMA_ENDPOINT ollama_model: str = DEFAULT_OLLAMA_MODEL context_limit: int = 1_024
def validate_preferences(preferences: Preferences) -> Preferences: if not all(isinstance(value, str) for value in ( preferences.microphone, preferences.trigger, preferences.style, preferences.asr_endpoint, preferences.ollama_endpoint, preferences.ollama_model, )): raise ValueError("string preferences must be TOML strings") if isinstance(preferences.context_limit, bool) or not isinstance(preferences.context_limit, int): raise ValueError("context_limit must be a TOML integer") if preferences.microphone == "": raise ValueError("microphone must be system-default or a device identifier") if not preferences.trigger: raise ValueError("trigger must not be empty") if preferences.style not in STYLES: raise ValueError(f"style must be one of: {', '.join(STYLES)}") if preferences.context_limit <= 0: raise ValueError("context_limit must be positive") validate_loopback_url(preferences.asr_endpoint) validate_loopback_url(preferences.ollama_endpoint) if not preferences.ollama_model: raise ValueError("ollama_model must not be empty") return preferences
def load_preferences(path: Path) -> Preferences: if not path.exists(): return validate_preferences(Preferences()) with path.open("rb") as file: data = tomllib.load(file) unknown = set(data) - set(Preferences.__dataclass_fields__) if unknown: raise ValueError(f"unknown preference: {sorted(unknown)[0]}") try: preferences = Preferences(**data) except TypeError as error: raise ValueError("invalid preferences TOML") from error return validate_preferences(preferences)
def save_preferences(path: Path, preferences: Preferences) -> None: preferences = validate_preferences(preferences) path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) content = "\n".join(f'{name} = {value!r}' for name, value in vars(preferences).items()) + "\n" descriptor, temporary_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=f".{path.name}.", dir=path.parent) try: with os.fdopen(descriptor, "w", encoding="utf-8") as file: file.write(content) file.flush() os.fsync(file.fileno()) os.replace(temporary_name, path) except BaseException: try: os.unlink(temporary_name) except FileNotFoundError: pass raise

from __future__ import annotations
import os import subprocess import sys import textwrap import unittest from pathlib import Path
ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
class SetupInstallDependenciesAcceptanceTests(unittest.TestCase): def test_explicit_install_reports_ordered_results_without_sensitive_fixture_data(self) -> None: script = textwrap.dedent( """ import contextlib import io from unittest.mock import patch from dictate.config import Preferences from dictate.installer import ComponentResult from dictate.service import ReadinessResult from dictate.cli import main
output = io.StringIO() with contextlib.redirect_stdout(output), contextlib.redirect_stderr(output), \\ patch('dictate.cli.current_platform', return_value=object()), \\ patch('dictate.cli.load_preferences', return_value=Preferences()), \\ patch('dictate.cli.check_readiness', return_value=ReadinessResult((), ())), \\ patch('dictate.cli.InstallerCoordinator') as coordinator: coordinator.return_value.install.return_value = ( ComponentResult('python-dependencies', 'retained'), ComponentResult('whisper-runtime', 'acquired'), ComponentResult('whisper-model', 'acquired'), ComponentResult('ollama-runtime', 'retained'), ComponentResult('ollama-model', 'retained'), ) assert main(['setup', '--install-dependencies']) == 0 value = output.getvalue() assert value.index('python-dependencies') < value.index('whisper-runtime') < value.index('whisper-model') assert 'unique-sensitive-fixture' not in value """ ) environment = os.environ | {"PYTHONPATH": str(ROOT / "src")} result = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", script], cwd=ROOT, env=environment, capture_output=True, text=True, check=False) self.assertEqual(0, result.returncode, result.stderr)
if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

from __future__ import annotations
import unittest from unittest.mock import patch
from dictate import bootstrap
class BootstrapTests(unittest.TestCase): def test_explicit_install_repairs_only_missing_declared_dependencies_before_cli(self) -> None: calls: list[tuple[str, ...]] = [] with patch("dictate.bootstrap.missing_dependencies", return_value=("sounddevice==0.5.5",)): result = bootstrap.main( ["setup", "--install-dependencies"], runner=lambda command: calls.append(tuple(command)) or 0, import_cli=lambda: lambda arguments: 7 if arguments == ["setup", "--install-dependencies"] else 1, ) self.assertEqual(7, result) self.assertEqual(1, len(calls)) self.assertEqual(("-m", "pip", "install", "sounddevice==0.5.5"), calls[0][1:])
def test_all_non_exact_install_commands_skip_dependency_repair(self) -> None: for arguments in (["setup"], ["doctor"], ["devices"], ["serve"], ["setup", "--other"]): with self.subTest(arguments=arguments): with patch("dictate.bootstrap.repair_dependencies") as repair: self.assertEqual(0, bootstrap.main(arguments, import_cli=lambda: lambda _arguments: 0)) repair.assert_not_called()
def test_failed_repair_does_not_import_cli(self) -> None: with patch("dictate.bootstrap.missing_dependencies", return_value=("pynput==1.8.2",)): self.assertEqual( 1, bootstrap.main(["setup", "--install-dependencies"], runner=lambda _command: 1, import_cli=lambda: self.fail("CLI must not import")), )
if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

from __future__ import annotations
import unittest
from dictate.platform.linux import LinuxAdapter from dictate.platform.macos import MacOSAdapter from dictate.platform.windows import WindowsAdapter
class Hotkey: def __init__(self) -> None: self.started = False self.stopped = False
def start(self) -> None: self.started = True def stop(self) -> None: self.stopped = True
class PlatformAdapterTests(unittest.TestCase): def test_all_platform_adapters_are_instantiable_and_fail_closed_for_target_safety(self) -> None: for adapter_type in (MacOSAdapter, WindowsAdapter, LinuxAdapter): with self.subTest(adapter=adapter_type.__name__): hotkeys: list[Hotkey] = []
def factory(*args: object) -> Hotkey: hotkey = Hotkey() hotkeys.append(hotkey) return hotkey
adapter = adapter_type(factory) self.assertTrue(adapter.microphone_permission().available) self.assertTrue(adapter.trigger_permission().available) self.assertFalse(adapter.placement_permission().available) self.assertFalse(adapter.context_permission().available) self.assertIsNone(adapter.snapshot_target()) self.assertFalse(adapter.target_matches(object())) self.assertFalse(adapter.insert_text(object(), "must-not-be-inserted"))
adapter.start_hotkey("right_alt", lambda: None, lambda: None) adapter.stop_hotkey() self.assertTrue(hotkeys[0].started) self.assertTrue(hotkeys[0].stopped)
if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

from __future__ import annotations
import unittest
from dictate.platform.linux import LinuxAdapter from dictate.platform.macos import MacOSAdapter from dictate.platform.windows import WindowsAdapter
class Hotkey: def __init__(self) -> None: self.started = False self.stopped = False
def start(self) -> None: self.started = True def stop(self) -> None: self.stopped = True
class PlatformAdapterTests(unittest.TestCase): def test_platform_runtime_acquisition_uses_one_documented_route(self) -> None: for adapter_type in (MacOSAdapter, WindowsAdapter, LinuxAdapter): with self.subTest(adapter=adapter_type.__name__): commands: list[tuple[str, ...]] = [] result = adapter_type(lambda *_args: Hotkey()).acquire_external_runtime( "whisper-runtime", lambda command: commands.append(tuple(command)) or True ) self.assertTrue(result.acquired) self.assertEqual(1, len(commands)) self.assertFalse(adapter_type(lambda *_args: Hotkey()).acquire_external_runtime("unknown", lambda _command: True).acquired)
def test_all_platform_adapters_are_instantiable_and_fail_closed_for_target_safety(self) -> None: for adapter_type in (MacOSAdapter, WindowsAdapter, LinuxAdapter): with self.subTest(adapter=adapter_type.__name__): hotkeys: list[Hotkey] = []
def factory(*args: object) -> Hotkey: hotkey = Hotkey() hotkeys.append(hotkey) return hotkey
adapter = adapter_type(factory) self.assertTrue(adapter.microphone_permission().available) self.assertTrue(adapter.trigger_permission().available) self.assertFalse(adapter.placement_permission().available) self.assertFalse(adapter.context_permission().available) self.assertIsNone(adapter.snapshot_target()) self.assertFalse(adapter.target_matches(object())) self.assertFalse(adapter.insert_text(object(), "must-not-be-inserted"))
adapter.start_hotkey("right_alt", lambda: None, lambda: None) adapter.stop_hotkey() self.assertTrue(hotkeys[0].started) self.assertTrue(hotkeys[0].stopped)
if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()
